I can use `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p -S -120` to grab the last 120 lines of the pane (the `-S` flag sets the start line relative to the end). I’ll pipe that through `grep -v '^\s*$'` to strip blank lines, then `tail -45` to focus on the most recent output where the final summaries should appear. This mirrors what I’ve done earlier when extracting output from glint sessions.

Adding an explicit marker `=== REAL TEST RESULT ===` before this block will make it clear in the combined output where the independent verification starts.

Putting this together, a single Bash tool call makes sense: first `sleep 60` to wait, then the tmux capture pipeline, then the echo marker, then the cd & python command. This way I get both the glint agent’s reported result and my own verification in one go, and I can immediately see if they match.

```
sleep 60 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p -S -120 | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -45; echo "=== REAL TEST RESULT ==="; cd /tmp/glint-complex && python3 test_calc.py 2>&1 | tail -3
```
